title: Integrated Rehabilitation & Monitoring Strategies in Cardiac Surgery
official: Integrated Rehabilitation & Monitoring Strategies in Cardiac Surgery: a Randomized Prospective Trial
summary:
People having heart surgery can face many physical and emotional challenges before and after the operation. They may need ongoing support to recover well, stay active, and avoid complications. The IReMoS study will evaluate a digital platform that uses ready-to-use technologies to support patients throughout their care journey, from home-based preparation before surgery to coaching after the operation and the final return home.

The IReMoS study is a prospective, single-centre randomized controlled trial that will start enrolling 223 participants. Adults aged 18-75 who are scheduled for planned heart surgery will be eligible if their surgery is at least two weeks after they give consent to take part. Participants in the intervention group will use the IReMoS digital platform that will provide virtual coaching for breathing and physical exercises, personalised educational information, and remote monitoring using a smartwatch and a smart shirt with built-in sensors.

The main goal of the study is to find out whether the use of the platform can reduce complications within three months after surgery. These complications include breathing problems, wound infections, worsening heart failure, and unexpected hospital readmissions. The study will also look at other outcomes, including death within three months, length of hospital stay, quality of life, anxiety, physical ability, and time spent moving. In addition, the researchers will assess how easy the platform is to use and how often technical problems occur.

Moreover, data collected in the study may also help future research develop "digital twins" of patients. These could eventually be used to predict how well a patient's physical and breathing functions will recover after surgery and identify those at higher risk of complications.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Elective cardiac surgery scheduled no sooner than two weeks after the hypothetical start of the pre-habilitation phase
* Possession of a smartphone compatible with the developed mobile application and an internet connection
* Willingness to use a smartwatch and a sensorized t-shirt
* Good knowledge of app language (level B2)
* Informed consent

Exclusion Criteria:

* Significant clinical conditions or comorbidities that prevent participation in the program or that may interfere with planned preoperative activities (e.g., severe motor limitations, psychological or cognitive disorders).
* Inability to use technology
* Patients with a language barrier (not able to speak or read the app language at a sufficient level)
* Urgent, emergency or salvage operations
